claims.text: Machine-learning-based molecular dynamics is a single intervention capable of overcoming current limitations in determining high-temperature solid and liquid properties of high-entropy alloys.
The machine-learning molecular dynamics model would use a carefully curated dataset of high-entropy alloys.
The intervention can determine melting temperature, enthalpy and entropy of fusion, volume change upon melting, and liquid thermodynamic properties.
The intervention can operate across a large compositional space.
Atomic interactions and atomic arrangements are the structural mediator connecting the simulations to the predicted thermodynamic properties.
A machine-learning algorithm learns patterns from molecular dynamics simulations.
Learning patterns from molecular dynamics permits accurate thermodynamic-property predictions across compositions and temperatures.
The intervention will improve accuracy relative to current experimental and computational methods.
The intervention will improve the availability of the listed thermodynamic properties relative to current methods.
The intervention will improve efficiency relative to current experimental and computational methods.
The intervention is applicable to high-entropy alloys containing 3–10 principal elements.
The intervention is applicable from 500 to 2000 K.
Model accuracy may be limited by the training dataset and by the complexity of high-entropy alloy systems.
Predictions should be compared with independent experimental reference data for the listed thermodynamic quantities.
A deviation greater than 10% from experimental reference data is the proposed falsification threshold.
